title: Now the people of the right: how fortunate they are!
subtitle: The second group, the righteous believers
then: After the foremost, the surah turns to {reward}those on the right, the righteous believers{/reward}. Maymun bin Mihran said they are lesser in rank than the foremost. The verse asks about them, then answers with a full picture of their home.
now: You are not the one who memorized the whole Quran or fasts every Monday. You pray, you try, you slip, you come back. {reward}This verse is about people like you{/reward}, and it calls them fortunate.
old: If I'm not one of the very best, Paradise isn't really for me.
new: The right is a real, honored place for ordinary striving believers.
try: Write down three good things you do regularly, and thank Allah for each one.

title: The lote tree, with its thorns removed.
subtitle: A familiar tree, made perfect
then: Many scholars said Sidr Makhdud is {reward}the kind without thorns{/reward}, and Ibn Abbas said it is laden with fruit. Ibn Kathir notes the lote tree of this life is thorny with little fruit; in Paradise it is the opposite. Mujahid said the Quraysh loved its shade.
now: Every good thing here has its thorn: the job with the long commute, the family you love who can also hurt you. {reward}A tree with the thorns taken out{/reward} is good without the sting.
old: Every blessing comes with a catch.
new: Allah can give me the fruit with the thorns removed.
try: Name one thorn in a blessing you have, and thank Allah for the blessing anyway.

title: Trees heavy with fruit, layer upon layer.
subtitle: Abundance stacked on abundance

row.title: talh
sub: a thorny shrub of the Hijaz

then: Talh was a large thorny shrub in the Hijaz whose shade the Quraysh liked. Mujahid said {reward}its fruits are piled on top of each other{/reward}. Many, including Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurayrah, said it means the banana tree.
now: You know a market stall piled with bananas, bunch over bunch, more than anyone could carry home. {reward}That kind of plenty{/reward} is the picture, drawn from a tree the listeners already knew.
old: Good things are always scarce and rationed.
new: Allah describes Paradise with plenty piled on plenty.
try: Share some of your food today with someone, so your table has a little of that plenty.

title: Shade that stretches farther than you can ride.
subtitle: A shade a rider crosses for a hundred years
then: The Prophet ﷺ said, as Al-Bukhari and Muslim recorded, that in Paradise is {reward}a tree whose shade a rider can travel for a hundred years without passing it{/reward}, and then recited this verse. To desert travelers, shade meant life.
now: The car parked in the sun all day, the bus stop with no roof, the summer walk home. You hunt for any patch of shade. {reward}This shade never ends.{/reward}
old: Relief in life always runs out quickly.
new: Allah's relief can be wider than any distance I could travel.
try: Next time you step into shade on a hot day, ask Allah for the extended shade.

title: Water that keeps on pouring.
subtitle: Constant water for a thirsty people
then: To the trees and the shade, the verse adds {reward}water flowing constantly{/reward}. For people living in a dry valley, running water that no one had to draw or carry was a picture of wealth and rest.
now: The water bill you check, the tap that sputters, the bottle you carry to the gym and ration. {reward}Water that keeps pouring{/reward} is ease without counting.
old: I take water for granted until it stops.
new: Water is a gift here and a promise there.
try: Make wudu slowly today and notice the water as a blessing.

title: Fruit in plenty, of every kind.
subtitle: Looks familiar, tastes new

row.title: looks familiar
sub: this is what we had before

then: Ibn Kathir says they will have {reward}plenty of fruits of various kinds{/reward}, and links it to the verse where the people of Paradise say this is what we were given before. The shape will look similar, but the taste is different.
now: You bite into the first mango of the season and it tastes better than you remembered. {reward}Paradise is that surprise, every time{/reward}, something familiar becoming new.
old: I've tasted everything this life has to offer.
new: Allah has joys waiting that only look familiar.
try: Eat one fruit slowly today and name one thing you love about its taste.

title: Never out of season, never out of reach.
subtitle: No end to the supply, no barrier to taking it
then: Ibn Kathir explains that {reward}the supply never runs out, winter or summer{/reward}, and nothing keeps them from reaching it. Two limits we know well, scarcity and barriers, are both removed.
now: Your favorite fruit is out of season, or it is there but too expensive this week, or it sits on a high shelf behind glass. {reward}Neither limit exists there.{/reward}
old: There is always something standing between me and what I want.
new: In Paradise, nothing stands between the believer and the good.
try: Remove one barrier for someone today: pay for a coffee, carry a bag, lend a charger.

title: Their beds are raised high.
subtitle: Comfort and honor together
then: The list of gifts for those on the right reaches their resting place: {reward}couches raised high{/reward}. A raised couch speaks of both comfort and honor, rest given to a welcome guest.
now: The thin mattress, the night shift, the sofa you fall asleep on with the TV still on. You rarely rest well. {reward}A raised bed of honor{/reward} is rest as a gift, not a collapse.
old: Rest is just what I grab when I'm too tired to go on.
new: Real rest is a gift Allah promises to those who strive.
try: Tonight, make wudu and say the bedtime dua before you lie down.

title: Allah creates them anew.
subtitle: A new creation, free of old wear and tear
then: Allah says {reward}We have produced them in a new creation{/reward}, with Himself as the One acting. After trees, water and couches, the verses turn to the people of Paradise themselves, made fresh.
now: You look in the mirror after a hard year: gray hairs, tired eyes, a back that aches in the morning. {idea}Age and wear are real here.{/idea} {reward}The verse promises a creation that is new.{/reward}
old: My body only goes one way: older and more tired.
new: Allah, who created me once, can create me anew.
try: Next time you notice a sign of age in yourself, say: O Allah, make what is coming better than what has passed.

title: Made pure and untouched.
subtitle: Freshness given as a gift
then: The description continues: Allah {reward}made them virgins{/reward}. The Quran states it briefly, as a gift of purity and freshness, and moves on. Allah is again the One who does the making.
now: So much around you is secondhand: the used car, the hand-me-down coat, a heart bruised by old hurts. {reward}The verse speaks of something given fresh{/reward}, never used up.
old: Nothing stays fresh; everything gets used up.
new: Allah can give something entirely fresh, untouched by any past hurt.
try: Ask Allah today to heal one old hurt in your heart and make it new.

title: Loving to their husbands, and of matching age.
subtitle: Love that fits, with no gap and no distance
then: The verse gives two qualities: {reward}devoted to their husbands, and of equal age{/reward}. It completes the picture of companionship among those on the right: love that is returned, and partners well matched.
now: A couple sits side by side on the sofa, each on a phone. Small distances grow quietly. {reward}The verse describes love without distance{/reward}, and you can start practicing it now.
old: Closeness in marriage fades, and that's just normal.
new: Warm, devoted love is part of what Allah calls reward.
try: Put your phone away for ten minutes tonight and give your full attention to someone you love.

title: All of this is for the people of the right.
subtitle: The list ends with whom it belongs to

row.title: for the right
sub: those who believed and did good

then: After the trees, shade, water, fruit and companions, the verse says plainly whom it is for: {reward}the companions of the right{/reward}. Not only the foremost, but the righteous believers just below them in rank.
now: You scroll past people who seem holier than you and think Paradise belongs to them. {reward}This verse addresses the gift to the right{/reward}, a crowd that ordinary believers can join.
old: This sounds wonderful, but it's for people better than me.
new: It is named for the people of the right, and I can be among them.
try: Do one ordinary good deed today with the intention of being among the people of the right.

title: A large company from the earlier ones.
subtitle: Many from the early generations are on the right
then: Earlier, the foremost were a crowd from the earlier ones and {trap}only a few from the later{/trap}. Here the people of the right are {reward}a large company from the earlier ones{/reward}, and the next verse balances it.
now: Your grandparents' generation prayed through hard times without apps, podcasts or lectures on demand. {reward}Many like them are in this company.{/reward} The verse honors those who came before you.
old: Older generations had simpler faith; it doesn't compare.
new: Many before me are among the right, and I can join their company.
try: Make dua today for your grandparents and the believers who came before them.

title: And a large company from the later ones too.
subtitle: The good news the Companions had hoped for
then: Abu Hurayrah reported that when the verses said {trap}only a few from the later ones{/trap}, it was hard for the Companions. Then these verses came, and the Prophet ﷺ said he hoped his Ummah would be {reward}half the people of Paradise{/reward}.
now: Sometimes you think the real believers lived long ago and you were born too late. {reward}This verse is about you, too.{/reward} A large company of the later ones means the door is wide.
old: I was born too late for the best of faith.
new: Allah promised a large company from the later ones, and that includes my generation.
try: Tell a friend one hopeful thing about faith today instead of a complaint about our times.
